Kropyvnytsky New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kirovohradska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kropyvnytsky — historically known as Elisavetgrad, then Zinovyevsk, Kirovo, and Kirovograd — saw its Jewish population grow from none in 1797 to almost 24,000 of 61,488 residents by 1897. In April 1881, Elisavetgrad was one of the first cities where that year's major wave of pogroms originated; a further pogrom struck in 1905, and in 1919, during the Russian Civil War, a pogrom claimed between 1,500 and 3,000 lives — one of the largest single pogrom death tolls documented in this collection. This, the newer of the city's two Jewish cemeteries, was established in 1896 and operated until 1951; its gravestones were looted during the 1941–44 German occupation, and the site was overbuilt with a cement factory.
